paragraphs.text: וַ֠יִּסְעוּ כָּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת הָעָֽם׃

i18n.en: And the whole congregation of the children of Yisra'el journeyed from the wilderness of Sin by their stages, according to the mouth of YHWH; and they camped at Refidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.

paragraphs.commentary: Arrival at Refidim; the wilderness-water-crisis sets up the Massah-Meribah aetiological-naming at v 7.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָם֙ עִם־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ תְּנוּ־לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תְּרִיבוּן֙ עִמָּדִ֔י מַה־תְּנַסּ֖וּן אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the people quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water, that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test YHWH?"

paragraphs.commentary: The *rîḇ* 'quarrel, contention' verb deployed twice; the lexeme will become the *Mĕrîḇâ* place-name at v 7. The *nsh* (Piʿel) 'to test' verb sets up the *Massâ* place-name.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּצְמָ֨א שָׁ֤ם הָעָם֙ לַמַּ֔יִם וַיָּ֥לֶן הָעָ֖ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הֶעֱלִיתָ֣נוּ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֛י וְאֶת־בָּנַ֥י וְאֶת־מִקְנַ֖י בַּצָּמָֽא׃

i18n.en: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people murmured against Moses, and said, "Why is this — that you have brought us up out of Mitsrayim to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"

paragraphs.text: וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה ע֥וֹד מְעַ֖ט וּסְקָלֻֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And Moses cried out to YHWH, saying, "What shall I do with this people? A little more and they will stone me."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְקַ֥ח אִתְּךָ֖ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Pass on before the people, and take with you some of the elders of Yisra'el; and your staff, with which you struck the Nile — take in your hand and go.

paragraphs.text: הִנְנִ֣י עֹמֵד֩ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ שָּׁ֥ם ׀ עַֽל־הַצּוּר֮ בְּחֹרֵב֒ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַצּ֗וּר וְיָצְא֥וּ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ מַ֖יִם וְשָׁתָ֣ה הָעָ֑ם וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Behold, I am standing before you there on the rock at Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out from it, and the people shall drink." And Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Yisra'el.

paragraphs.commentary: *ha-ṣṣûr bĕ-ḥōrēḇ* 'the rock at Horeb' — explicit localization at the divine-mountain. The *ṣûr* 'rock' lexeme has cross-corpus reach as a divine-epithet (Deut 32:4, 32:18 YHWH as *ṣûr*; Isa 26:4; Ps 18:2, 31:3, 62:7); the Rock-as-divine-epithet tradition is a documented Hebrew Bible feature. Operational disavowals at the central entry `maśśah-merivah-testing-contention-place-name-aetiological-cross-corpus`: no Christological pre-resolution of the rock (against 1 Cor 10:4 'the rock was Christ'); no engineered-installation Sitchin/Raëlian-canon reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֔וֹם מַסָּ֖ה וּמְרִיבָ֑ה עַל־רִ֣יב ׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְעַ֨ל נַסֹּתָ֤ם אֶת־יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲיֵ֧שׁ יְהוָ֛ה בְּקִרְבֵּ֖נוּ אִם־אָֽיִן׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he called the name of the place Massah (Testing) and Meribah (Quarreling), because of the quarreling of the children of Yisra'el and because of their testing of YHWH, saying, "Is YHWH in our midst, or not?"

paragraphs.commentary: **The Massah-Meribah aetiological-naming**: *wa-yyiqrāʾ šēm ha-māqôm massâ ū-mĕrîḇâ* 'and he called the name of the place Massah (Testing) and Meribah (Quarreling)'. The doubled-naming establishes the foundational covenantal-recall paradigm of Israelite-disbelief. Cross-corpus to Deut 6:16, 9:22, 33:8, Ps 95:8-9, Heb 3:7-19, 4:1-11.

i18n.en: And Amaleq came and fought with Yisra'el at Refidim.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Amalek-attack initiation-verse.** Amaleq's attack at Refidim establishes the Amalek-as-perennial-enemy theological-pattern. See the central entry `amalek-perennial-enemy-ex-17-deut-25-1-sam-15-esther-cross-corpus` for the cross-corpus chain (Deut 25:17-19 → 1 Sam 15 → Esther) and the operational disavowals against modern political weaponization, Christian-supersessionist inversion, and Sitchin/Raëlian fringe-readings.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ בְּחַר־לָ֣נוּ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְצֵ֖א הִלָּחֵ֣ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק מָחָ֗ר אָנֹכִ֤י נִצָּב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה וּמַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Moses said to Yehoshua, "Choose men for us and go out, fight with Amaleq. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of the Elohim in my hand."

paragraphs.commentary: *Yehošuaʿ* — first appearance of the future leader. The WoH-Translation preserves the Hebrew transliteration 'Yehoshua' per the project's Genesis-precedent register rather than smoothing to the English-tradition 'Joshua'. *maṭṭê hā-ʾĕlōhîm* 'the staff of the Elohim' — the divine-instrument designation.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽמַר־לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וְח֔וּר עָל֖וּ רֹ֥אשׁ הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua did as Moses had said to him, to fight with Amaleq; and Moses, Aharon, and Chur went up to the top of the hill.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥ים מֹשֶׁ֛ה יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנִ֛יחַ יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֥ר עֲמָלֵֽק׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Moses raised his hand, that Yisra'el prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amaleq prevailed.

paragraphs.commentary: The raised-hands-of-Moses ritual-instrument pattern. The midrashic-rabbinic tradition (Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael, Amalek 1; m. Rosh Hashanah 3:8) reads the raised-hands not as magical-instrument but as Israel-orientation-to-divine-presence.

paragraphs.text: וִידֵ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ כְּבֵדִ֔ים וַיִּקְחוּ־אֶ֛בֶן וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ תַחְתָּ֖יו וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב עָלֶ֑יהָ וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וְח֜וּר תָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו מִזֶּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וּמִזֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י יָדָ֛יו אֱמוּנָ֖ה עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: And the hands of Moses were heavy; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it; and Aharon and Chur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
And Yehoshua disabled Amaleq and his people with the edge of the sword.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּתֹ֨ב זֹ֤את זִכָּרוֹן֙ בַּסֵּ֔פֶר וְשִׂ֖ים בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּֽי־מָחֹ֤ה אֶמְחֶה֙ אֶת־זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Write this as a memorial in the book, and place it in the ears of Yehoshua: for I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amaleq from under the heavens."

paragraphs.commentary: **The divine-curse-of-Amalek**: *māḥōh ʾemḥeh ʾeṯ zēḵer ʿămālēq mit-taḥaṯ ha-šāmāyim* 'I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amaleq from under the heavens'. The doubled-verb *māḥōh ʾemḥeh* deploys the same emcheh-erasure root as Gen 6:7 (the Flood-erasure); the existing entry `emcheh` documents the cross-corpus root-deployment. The genocidal-language of the Hebrew Bible's Amalek-curse is preserved on the surface; the WoH-Translation explicitly disavows any modern political identification with the Amalek-figure (see the central entry).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ נִסִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And Moses built an altar and called its name YHWH-Nissi (YHWH is my banner).

paragraphs.commentary: *YHWH nissî* 'YHWH is my banner' — altar-name; one of the YHWH-compound altar-names of the Pentateuch (cf. YHWH-Yir'eh at Gen 22:14; YHWH-Shalom at Judg 6:24; YHWH-Tzidqenu at Jer 23:6).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יָד֙ עַל־כֵּ֣ס יָ֔הּ מִלְחָמָ֥ה לַיהוָ֖ה בַּֽעֲמָלֵ֑ק מִדֹּ֖ר דֹּֽר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he said, "For a hand is upon the throne of YAH: YHWH will have war with Amaleq from generation to generation."

paragraphs.commentary: **The textually-difficult closing**: MT preserves *kî-yāḏ ʿal-kēs yāh* 'for a hand is upon the throne of YAH' (with the *yāh* shortened-tetragrammaton, the only YH occurrence in Exodus); the LXX/Samaritan/Syriac variant reads *nēs* 'banner' (harmonizing with the YHWH-Nissi altar-name at v 15). See the overlay entry `kes-yah-vs-nes-yah-textual-variant-exodus-17-16-overlay`. The MT *lectio difficilior* is preserved per Childs 1974, Propp 1999, Sarna 1991.
